title: pmx event clusters and constraints v1
description: The document data/datasets/<name>/clusters/clusters.json: the cross-venue EventCluster records and the intra-venue Constraint records computed at build time and sealed with the dataset. The hand-written override file validates against #/$defs/override_file. Every cluster records why it matched, and a cluster whose match needed resolved_at_ms or a human carries asof: false and never reaches an agent. This document carries no dataset_hash: its own bytes are an input to that hash (CONTRACTS_V2 4.3 walks clusters/), so a field holding it could never be filled (ruling R128). CONTRACTS_V2 section 16.3.

resolution_tolerance_ms.description: The tolerance the matcher applies to resolution dates. It is on the analysis path only: a grouping whose formation consulted resolved_at_ms in any way, as a stored reason or as a filter, stores a resolution_date reason and therefore carries asof: false (CONTRACTS_V2 16.3, ruling R132).

match_reason.description: One stored reason a match was made, with the score it contributed. asof is false for a reason a live agent could not have computed at now_ms (a resolution date, a human override); a cluster is asof only when every one of its reasons is.

allOf.description: A resolution date proximity and a human override are hindsight by construction (CONTRACTS_V2 7.9 forbids resolved_at_ms in a view), so neither may claim to be as-of.

event_cluster.description: Markets on one real-world event, grouped by the deterministic conservative matcher of CONTRACTS_V2 16.3. Never a label to an agent.

resolution_span_ms.description: max(resolved_at_ms) - min(resolved_at_ms) over the members, and -1 on an as-of cluster, whose formation never read a resolution date (ruling R132). Analysis recomputes the span from the dataset when it wants it.

allOf.description: A hand-forced cluster is never as-of and always carries its manual reason.
An as-of cluster is matched by content only, so it never read a resolution date and cannot report a span (CONTRACTS_V2 16.3, ruling R132).

constraint.description: A logical relation between the prices of two or more markets, from a Kalshi event ticker, a threshold ladder, a venue-declared duplicate or complement, or a manual override. market_ids is ordered by the relation's own semantics: (antecedent, consequent) for implies, ascending threshold for monotone_ladder, canonical market order otherwise.

cluster_id.description: The cluster this relation lives inside, or null when it stands alone. When it is not null every id of market_ids is a member of that cluster: the matcher extends the cluster rather than filing a constraint against a partial one (CONTRACTS_V2 16.3, ruling R143). The check is across records, so tests/test_contract_schemas.py asserts it.

allOf.description: implies and complement are binary relations; a third member would make the residual of 16.3 undefined.
Only a ladder has a direction; the other three residuals are sums and differences.
A hand-written constraint is never as-of.

override_file.description: data/datasets/<name>/clusters/overrides.json: the hand-written review, sealed with the dataset and hashed into overrides_sha256. force adds a grouping the matcher missed, forbid removes a false positive it made. Both are hindsight, so every cluster they touch carries asof: false.
